answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond, then assign its first jobs through a beacon lottery weighted by that bond and an anchor of established counterparties willing to vouch for its behavior. If the agent completes work honestly, the bond returns and its reputation grows; if it defaults or colludes, the bond is slashed and vouchers lose standing. A yarrow seed phrase in the onboarding flow can mark this trial stage. Sybil farms must lock real capital across identities and risk losing it, making mass creation costly rather than free.
